- A worked example showing per-call token counts, any rounding quantum applied, and how session-level bundling reduces charges when the same context is reused within a short window.
- How a committed seat credit / seat-offset would be applied month-to-month if Acme buys 50 committed seats but only 45 are active on average.

Eli —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a short pilot scope (pilot_scope.xlsx) and looped in Ben (billing) and Priyom (pricing/packaging) to back the math. High level summary up front:

- Token quantum: Redwood bills tokens in a 100-token quantum for per-request rounding by default; we also offer session-level bundling where requests from the same session within a 60s window are aggregated before rounding.
- Context bundling: if a session reuses KV cache/prefix (embeddings + summary) within the bundling window we only count the delta tokens generated/ingested after caching benefit is considered.
- Seat offsets / committed seats: committed seats act as a monthly credit pool. If you commit 50 seats and average 45 active, the leftover 5 seats are consumed as credits against your consumed token/seat bill at the contracted offset rate. Unused committed seats are not forfeited during the monthly billing period but are reconciled per contract (we can specify true-up cadence).

Quick worked example (illustrative):
- 50 clinicians on pilot, average active in a day: 45.
- Typical call: user prompt 120 tokens + model reply 180 tokens = 300 tokens per call.
- Without bundling, per-call rounding to 100-token quantum => 300 -> 300 (already a multiple).
- With many 1-turn calls that include same 2k-token patient summary cached: we count the 2k summary once per session window if reused, then subsequent calls only bill delta (~300). If two calls from same session within 60s, aggregation would count 600 tokens before applying quantum.
- Committed seat offset: assume 50-seat commitment gives a 40% seat credit (example). If the raw seat-related billing would be $X/month, the committed-credit reduces seat-line by 40% up to 50 seats. Any active seats beyond commitments are billed at list seat rate.

Ben will send a line-item invoice example with the math + contract wording suggestions. If that looks fine, we can draft the clause for the SOW around seat true-up and rounding window.

Would you prefer a short recorded example invoice or a live call Thursday?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

Forwarding a worked example below — I've kept the math conservative for procurement. Note I added a tiny smoothing rule we apply for pilots to avoid noisy microbilling.

--- forwarded message ---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2029 09:30:00 -08:00
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Subject: Worked invoice example for Acme (pilot)

Ben's worked invoice (sample month):
- Commitment: 50 seats committed at $1,200/seat/mo (list) -> credit: 40% per-seat offset -> effective seat-credit value = $480/seat/mo applied against seat-line.
- Actual active seats (average): 45 -> applied credits used = 45 * $480 = $21,600.
- Token usage (example): total raw tokens generated/ingested in month = 120,000,000 tokens.
  - We apply session bundling for repeated KV reuse: deduped tokens counted = 90,000,000 tokens.
  - Per-request rounding quantum: 100 tokens -> billed token units = ceil(90,000,000 / 100) = 900,000 units.
  - Token unit price (pilot discount): $0.0009/unit -> token line = $810.
- Pilot smoothing: for pilots under 6 months we floor per-account token line to $5,000/mo to avoid tiny bills due to heavy caching; this is a negotiable term.
- Invoice lines shown: Seat list, Seat credits (negative line), Token usage, Pilot floor (if applicable), VAT/region tax.

Notes / clarifications:
- Rounding is applied at the aggregation stage (post-bundling). We do not round individual sub-token fragments — we run aggregation first, then quantum rounding. That helps keep high-reuse workloads cheaper.
- If you want per-request determinism (no bundling) we can lock quantum at call-level but that increases token units.
- Seat true-up cadence: monthly by default; quarterly or annual true-up can be added to the SOW.

Suggested contract language snippet (example):
"Committed Seats: Customer agrees to purchase 50 committed seats. Committed-seat credits are applied monthly against the Seat Usage invoice line. Any unused committed seats in a given month shall be applied as credits and will be reconciled per the True-Up cadence described in Section X."

If you want, Priyom can propose two packaging options (strict per-call billing vs bundling with smoothing floor) and we can present side-by-side TCO for 12 months.

Ben Carter
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
